passage:
Scientists placed microphones under the ocean to record whale songs and ship noise. The recordings were played in a museum.
Visitors heard deep calls, clicks, and long sounds that seemed almost musical. Then they heard the noise of ships crossing the same water.
A guide explained that sound travels far underwater. For some animals, noise can make communication harder.
A student left the exhibit thinking about pollution differently. Pollution was not only trash or dirty water. It could also be sound.
The ocean may look empty from above, but it is full of signals. Human activity can interrupt conversations we are only beginning to understand.
